items.title: Over 80pct of haj depositors yet to meet RM15,000 savings threshold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 80 per cent of about 4.1 million depositors registered for haj have savings of less than RM15,000, which is the minimum amount required to maintain their current queue eligibility after the transition period ends. Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) said the figure indicates that while a large portion of depositors already have a haj queue position, they have yet to reach a sufficient level of savings in preparation for when an offer is extended. The "first-come, first-served" principle is maintained among depositors who meet the minimum RM15,000 savings requirement, based on their respective haj registration date and time.

items.title: HSIS Heart Centre handles 69 cardiac intervention cases in a single day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Sultan Idris Shah Hospital (HSIS) Heart Centre in Serdang successfully managed 69 cardiology intervention cases in a single day on Friday. The Health Ministry said the facility handled 45 per cent of all cardiac intervention cases across the ministry's 10 heart centres. High-tech procedures carried out included four RotaPro Rotational Atherectomy cases and three Intravascular Lithotripsy cases.

items.title: Fahmi says misleading online health ad complaints will be sent to MCMC for review
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Complaints about online health advertisements and promotions that may violate regulations and mislead the public will be referred to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC). Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the matter was among the issues raised during his meeting with representatives from medical associations and healthcare experts in Kuala Lumpur today. He said the meeting was held to hear the views, suggestions and concerns raised by the representatives and medical experts.

items.title: SAR operation for missing anglers at One Fathom Bank near Pulau Ketam ends with no new leads
items.summary: KLANG, Sept 20 — The search and rescue (SAR) operation for anglers reported missing at One Fathom Bank near Pulau Ketam since last Monday was terminated yesterday after no new leads or discoveries were reported. Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) operations officer Lieutenant Mohd Azlee Zainal said the six-day operation covered a radius of 3,887 square nautical miles in the waters of Selangor and Perak. “The operation until 7 pm last night did not find any new leads or the one angler who is still missing.

items.title: Haze watch: 21 areas nationwide wake up to unhealthy air
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Haze continued to cloud parts of the country this morning, with 21 areas recording unhealthy air quality as of 8am. Johor also saw unhealthy air quality in Larkin, which recorded 162, and Pasir Gudang at 155. Another 41 areas recorded moderate air quality, including Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur and Miri in Sarawak, both at 99, and Politeknik Kota Kinabalu at 98.

items.title: Ed Sheeran set to return to stage after Palestinian controversy
items.summary: PHILADELPHIA: Chanting protesters greeted concertgoers Saturday in Philadelphia ahead of pop superstar Ed Sheeran's first show since his tour plunged into turmoil ignited by his opening act's pro-Palestinian comments. Rapper Macklemore was booted from Sheeran's US Loop Tour on Monday after the owners of stadiums hosting upcoming shows objected to his shouting "Free Palestine" onstage in New Jersey earlier this month. Sheeran, 35, has denied being behind the decision to remove Macklemore, blaming the tour promoter.

items.title: Serian tops unhealthy air quality readings as 21 areas affected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Twenty-one areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 8am today. In Johor, two areas recorded unhealthy API readings — Larkin (162) and Pasir Gudang (155). Meanwhile, 41 areas recorded moderate API readings, including Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (99), Miri, Sarawak (99) and Politeknik, Kota Kinabalu (98).

items.title: Sabah tourism bucks the slump talk with 4.1pc rise
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 20 — Sabah tourist arrivals rose 4.1 per cent from January to August, disproving talk of a slump in the state’s tourism sector. State Tourism, Culture and Environment Assistant Minister Dr Andi Md Shamsureezal Mohd Sainal said there had been an increase in both international and domestic arrivals during the period. “The talk that Sabah’s tourism is declining is not true at all,” he said after officiating the opening ceremony of the Malaysian Association of Tour and Travel Agents (Matta) Fair Sabah at the Sabah International Convention Centre, here, Saturday.

items.title: #NSTviral: 'Mak Cik' impresses netizens with 4km run in 30 minutes [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 73-year-old woman has impressed social media users after a video posted on Threads showed her running 4.07km in 30 minutes. The post by @dausyusofjr showed her completing the run at a pace of seven minutes and 21 seconds per kilometre, drawing admiration from commenters who said they would struggle to keep up. the poster wrote in the caption.

items.title: Fire Dept: SAR launched after hiker slips down slope and becomes separated from group in Gua Musang
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 20 — The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) launched a search and rescue (SAR) operation last night for a male hiker who became separated from his group in the jungle near Kem Tudung Periuk, Gua Musang. A Kelantan JBPM spokesman said the Operations Control Centre (PGO) contacted the victim, despite unstable phone coverage in the area, and he shared his location through WhatsApp. The Gua Musang Fire and Rescue Station sent a Fire Rescue Tender and a Hilux vehicle to the location, 116 kilometres from the station.

items.title: Trump says will not tolerate attempts to slow AI growth
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Saturday lashed out at critics of artificial intelligence and data centers, saying he would not allow the "destruction" of the industry and announcing the creation of a new government "AI Force." Trump – who finds himself out of step with growing public skepticism over AI and dire safety warnings from AI industry leaders – said liberals want the "decimation, or destruction, of AI." Trump added, without explaining, that he was creating an "AI Force" that would be tasked with "looking for BAD" actors, and would soon announce an AI coordinator or "Czar."

items.title: Bajau boat builder keeps lepa tradition alive
items.summary: The Kg Tonggulangan villager has built about 30 lepa boats, each taking about a year to complete and measuring about 11m long. Its elaborate design also carries cultural meaning. [[nid:1536590]] Biskal said the Bajau community once used lepa boats for fishing and travelling at sea, but they have since been replaced by modern speedboats.

items.title: UM121 start of a new chapter
items.summary: UNIVERSITI Malaya (UM) will focus on improving its global standing while sustaining academic excellence, research and societal contributions as it marks its 121st anniversary, says Vice-Chancellor Professor Datuk Seri Dr Noor Azuan Abu Osman. While global rankings are not UM's sole focus, the university recognises their importance in shaping how higher education institutions are perceived internationally, he said. Noor Azuan said UM's 121-year history carries a great responsibility to remain relevant to the nation and deliver tangible benefits to society.

items.title: Perkeso officer goes door to door to find those in need
items.summary: WHEN most people are still turning over in bed, Muhammad Abrar Othman, or Abrar as he's better known, has already risen and started his day. Abrar's job is to find them. A PERKESO Skuad Prihatin Sinergi officer, Abrar, 32, rises around 4.30am and is usually at his desk by 5.30am, going through cases that come in overnight.

items.title: Old photo, Facebook search reunite friends after four decades [WATCH]
items.summary: When Devaki Rani Munusamy and Rohani Ambri, both 73, met recently, they held onto each other tightly, promising never to lose touch again. Once school ended, we went our separate ways, but we still spoke to each other whenever we could," said Devaki Rani. She was already driving by then," said Devaki Rani.

items.title: Cuba works to restore power after another blackout
items.summary: HAVANA: Cuba worked Saturday to restore power after its seventh major blackout of the year, as the communist-run island grappled with woes triggered by a US fuel blockade. This latest nationwide outage, the 12th since late 2024, occurred after a failure in transmission lines paired with "unstable weather conditions," state-run utility UNE said Friday. UNE said 48 percent of its customers in Havana had regained power on Saturday.

items.title: 'UM must continue building on legacy'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Malaya (UM) must continue building on its legacy by expanding its national impact, adapting to student needs and nurturing future leaders, according to alumni and current students. UM chief of staff Maheran Zainal Abidin said the institution had evolved significantly since she graduated from the Faculty of Economics and Administration in 1999. "I hope my contributions, however small, can support UM's growth and excellence."

items.title: Haze leaves food delivery riders working through health risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Food delivery riders are forced to keep working through the haze despite health risks as limited occupational safety guidance leaves many with little choice but to carry on. North-South Initiatives executive director and co-founder Adrian Pereira said riders who fell ill or were unable to work due to the poor air quality may have no guaranteed compensation, making it difficult for them to simply stop working. Pereira said the lack of clear guidance was concerning as prolonged exposure to haze could affect workers in ways that might not be immediately apparent.

items.title: Santap Lah: Ready-to-eat meals from Malaysia’s Michelin selected restaurants at a CAFé by 7-Eleven near you
items.summary: This is what sparked the birth of Santap Lah, a newly launched brand of microwaveable meals curated, prepared and approved by chefs from Michelin recognised restaurants in Malaysia. “After asking around, several chefs showed interest and that was when we started developing recipes for the meals,” he said. Chang also has a contact who operated a retort food manufacturing facility to produce and pack the meals.

items.title: Thousands protest inaction over climate crisis in Switzerland
items.summary: LAUSANNE: Several thousand people marched in the Swiss cities of Geneva and Lausanne on Saturday to protest government inaction in the face of global warming. ", AFP journalists noted. The larger demonstration was at Lausanne, where organisers said at least 8,000 had taken part.

items.title: Bersatu urges RoS to decide on complaint against PN soon
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Bersatu hopes the Registrar of Societies (RoS) will decide soon on a complaint filed by the party last month over alleged breaches by Perikatan Nasional (PN) leaders. Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the party had raised eight key matters which it claimed had been violated or disregarded by PN leaders. RoS had previously confirmed receiving a formal complaint from Bersatu over the party's alleged exclusion from a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16.

items.title: Muhyiddin: Pas decided to end political cooperation with Bersatu
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Pas decided to end its political cooperation with Bersatu, said Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin. "Pas made the decision not to continue cooperating. On June 9, Pas officially ended its political cooperation with Bersatu with immediate effect.

items.title: Muhyiddin denies acquittal linked to talks with PH
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has denied that his acquittal on four charges involving RM200 million was linked to efforts to forge cooperation with Pakatan Harapan (PH) to form a new political alignment. "Instead, it involved court proceedings over the charges I faced. High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin said the prosecution had not provided reasons for discontinuing the four charges and exercised the court's discretion in Muhyiddin's favour.

items.title: Muhyiddin: Bersatu has held talks with several parties on new political alliance
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has confirmed that the party has held talks with several political parties on efforts to form a new political alignment and chart its direction for the 16th General Election (GE16). "Bersatu is open to exploring cooperation with other parties that respect the basic principles of Bersatu's struggle. Muhyiddin said Bersatu could not favour any particular party when determining the form of cooperation for a new political alignment.

items.title: Education Ministry aims to strengthen Korean language skills among students
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry aims to strengthen Korean language proficiency among students in the country under its international language subject initiative. TIKL is among nine technical secondary schools (SMT) nationwide that have been rebranded as Technical Fully Residential Schools (SBP-T). The other eight are SMT Alor Setar in Kedah, SMT Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra in Penang, SMT Tuanku Jaa'far in Negri Sembilan, SMT Bukit Piatu in Melaka, SMT Kuala Terengganu in Terengganu, SMT Kuantan in Pahang, SMT Johor Bahru in Johor and SMT Sejingkat in Sarawak.

items.title: Health ads that breach rules to be referred to MCMC, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Complaints about online health advertisements and promotions that may breach regulations or mislead the public will be referred to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for review and further action. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the issue was among those raised during his meeting with representatives of medical associations and healthcare experts here today. He said the meeting was held to hear views, suggestions and concerns from the representatives and medical experts.

items.title: Bersatu will not go solo in GE16, says Muhyiddin
items.summary: Muhyiddin said any decision taken by the party must be based on its principles and interests. "Almost everyone who gave me their views said Bersatu cannot move alone. Muhyiddin said in deciding on coalition partners, Bersatu must choose those who respect the party's struggle and value its contributions.

items.title: Sirim's NEW TDM Project to advance digital manufacturing
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Malaysia's tool, die and mould (TDM) industry is set to enter a new phase of digital transformation and global competitiveness with the launch of NEW TDM Project next month. Implemented under the 13th Malaysia Plan and the New Industrial Master Plan 2030, the initiative aims to strengthen the TDM ecosystem through digital engineering, talent development and advanced manufacturing capabilities. Sirim president and group chief executive officer Nik Sazali Nik Hussin said TDM 2.0 laid a strong foundation for the industry, while the NEW TDM Project would accelerate its transformation.

items.title: Diana revelations, Harry return give Charles a testing week
items.summary: Britain's King Charles faces a trying few days, from screaming headlines raking over reportedly cruel comments about his late ex-wife Diana to his errant son Harry re-entering public life at an event in London. The Daily Mail, which is serialising the book, said on its website: "King at war." The Daily Telegraph said "Palace hits back at Diana's brother," on its front page, while the Sun said: "Recollections may vary... again," in reference to a previous royal response to criticism from Harry and his American wife Meghan.

items.title: Keep subsidies for consumers in Budget 2027, says ministry
items.summary: BATU KAWAN: The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry hopes allocations for subsidies, consumer affairs and the people's well-being will continue to receive due attention in the 2027 Budget, despite fiscal challenges arising from the rising cost of fuel subsidies. He said the ministry hoped subsidy allocations, including those for the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS), cooking oil and the Price Standardisation Programme for Sabah and Sarawak, could be maintained. However, he said the government's targeted subsidy reforms had enabled subsidies to continue reaching eligible groups despite rising costs.

items.title: Hung Parliament threatens Mindanao's autonomy progress
items.summary: Twelve years after the 2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB) between the Philippine government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) —which was facilitated by Malaysia —the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) held its first parliamentary election on Sept 14. Either the Manila-backed Bangsamoro Federalist Party or the MILF-backed United Bangsamoro Justice Party will need to cobble together a coalition with minor parties to form the new BARMM government by month's end. Such uncompleted tasks will now fall on the newly elected Parliament and regional government to address.

items.title: Denmark hails 'binding' Greenland deal with Trump
items.summary: COPENHAGEN: Denmark on Saturday hailed a "binding" deal announced by US President Donald Trump to give Washington "permanent control" over Greenland's security and bar Russian and Chinese bases from the Arctic territory. Denmark and Greenland – an autonomous Danish territory – both hailed the deal and said they would sign it on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York next week. Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said Saturday the potential signing meant "next week could be a good week."

items.title: NST Leader: What led to Tasik Bera land grab?
items.summary: Land encroachment is as ancient as land ownership, going back thousands of years. About 2,000 years ago, Rome established rights over land ownership and strict property boundaries, penalising accidental or deliberate construction of walls over a neighbour's boundary. In the United States, this historical dispute still simmers: the 19th century Wild West land grab to open up millions of hectares of Indigenous land for white and immigrant settlers.

items.title: One killed, six seriously injured in three-vehicle crash in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: Kota Tinggi district police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the deceased, Chua Bing Xuan, 26, was a passenger in a Perodua Myvi. "The crash involved a Perodua Myvi driven by a 21-year-old man with four passengers, a Proton Exora driven by a 56-year-old man with one passenger, and a Mazda CX-30 driven by a 30-year-old man. "The driver and all passengers of the Perodua Myvi and Proton Exora were seriously injured and taken to Sultan Ismail Hospital (HSI) in Johor Baru, Pasir Gudang Hospital (HPG) and Kota Tinggi Hospital (HKT) for treatment," he said in a statement today.

items.title: SAR for missing One Fathom Bank angler called off after six days
items.summary: KLANG: The search and rescue (SAR) operation for anglers reported missing at One Fathom Bank near Pulau Ketam since last Monday was called off today after no new leads or discoveries were reported. Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) operations officer Lieutenant Mohd Azlee Zainal said the six-day operation covered a radius of 3,887 square nautical miles in the waters of Selangor and Perak. "The operation until 7pm last night did not find any new leads or the one angler who is still missing.

items.title: 'Here's how to write it': Akmal dares Nga to honour resignation pledge after Loke quits
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh has reminded Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming of his earlier pledge to resign, following DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke's announcement that he was stepping down as transport minister. Earlier, Loke announced his resignation as transport minister following the decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak conditional house arrest. However, Loke said other DAP ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the Unity Government.

items.title: Bukit Aman’s USJT takes over probe into viral theatre clip mocking Rukun Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The Classified Criminal Investigation Unit (USJT) of the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has taken over the investigation into a viral theatre performance video that allegedly mocks the five principles of the Rukun Negara and contains racially sensitive remarks. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed that the report on the case was lodged at the Jalan Tun Razak Police Station under the Wangsa Maju District Police Headquarters (IPD) at 8.30pm yesterday. He said a complainant lodged the report after spotting a stage performance video clip uploaded by the Instagram account @THEFEVERKINETIC.

items.title: PM Anwar flags off Malaysia Sarong Music Run 2026 at Twin Towers, joins three‑kilometre walk
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today flagged off the Malaysia Sarong Music Run 2026 in front of the Petronas Twin Towers here. Speaking at the event, Anwar thanked participants of all ages and backgrounds for joining the run and helping promote healthy living in the community. Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing.

items.title: Police yet to confirm if Ipoh pre-dawn crash involving 15 vehicles linked to illegal racing
items.summary: BATU GAJAH, Sept 19 — Police have yet to confirm whether a group of motorcyclists involved in a fatal accident involving 12 motorcycles and three cars at Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here early today were linked to illegal racing. Perak deputy police chief DCP Mohammad Azlin Sadari said police needed to record statements from nine injured motorcyclists still receiving treatment in hospital to determine what happened before and during the crash. Meanwhile, Mohammad Azlin said dashcam footage had helped police identify two men suspected of threatening a driver with a stick along Jalan Ipoh-Gopeng, Simpang Pulai here.

items.title: Loke to resign as Transport Minister, DAP stays in Anwar’s government after Najib’s conditional pardon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Anthony Loke Siew Fook will step down from his position as Transport Minister in the Pakatan Harapan-led unity government following the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. He said DAP will remain in the federal unity government, with its ministers continuing to serve in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s Cabinet. Loke added that he would submit his resignation letter to Anwar soon.

items.title: Air quality dips nationwide, Sarawak records seven unhealthy API readings, Klang Valley four, Johor three
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — A total of 17 areas nationwide recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4 pm today. According to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Sarawak recorded seven areas with unhealthy readings, namely IPD Serian (178), Kuching (171), Sri Aman (168), Samarahan (164), Sibu (157), Sarikei (152) and Bintulu (106). Meanwhile, 38 other areas recorded moderate readings, while 12 areas recorded good air quality.

items.title: Police probe Rompin religious school hostel assault, five senior students freed on bail
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 19 — A mother has claimed that her 14-year-old son and another Form Two student were assaulted by five students at a religious school hostel in Bukit Ibam, Rompin, resulting in injuries to various parts of their bodies. Siti Rohani Yusof, 40, said the first incident occurred at about midnight on Sept 12 when the two students were called into a hostel room, had their heads covered and were allegedly beaten, with her son assaulted for about two hours and his friend for about two and a half hours. She said the senior students allegedly kicked, pinched, slapped and punched her son, besides hitting him with a broomstick.

items.title: Sarawak, Penang to get greater focus in Malaysia fertility push, says women’s minister
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 19 — Sarawak and Penang will receive greater focus under the government’s efforts to improve Malaysia’s fertility rate and address the country’s low birth rate, said Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri. She said the ministry planned to place greater emphasis on fertility-related programmes next year, including measures to support couples facing difficulties conceiving. Nancy said the ministry’s efforts would include programmes to assist couples facing difficulties having children, including initiatives under the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), such as in-vitro fertilisation (IVF).

items.title: Najib’s conditional pardon has not strained unity government, says DPM Zahid
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Relations among the parties that make up the unity government remain good following the Pardons Board’s decision involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said that in managing government affairs, all parties continue to act professionally, with Cabinet decisions being made collectively. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said the decision of the Pardons Board regarding Najib, which received the consent of His Majesty, was bound by provisions of the Federal Constitution.

items.title: DAP leaders gather for emergency CEC meeting over Najib’s conditional pardon
items.summary: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke arrives at DAP headquarters in Kuala Lumpur September 19, 2026. DAP national deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming arrives at DAP headquarters in Kuala Lumpur September 19, 2026. Hannah Yeoh arrives at DAP headquarters in Kuala Lumpur September 19, 2026.

items.title: Fourteen of 20 banks now offer reducing balance hire-purchase financing, says Armizan
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Sept 19 — Fourteen of the 20 banking institutions providing hire-purchase financing had begun offering customers the reducing balance method as of Sept 18, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. He said the remaining six banking institutions are expected to complete the transition to the new method by December 31 at the latest, following engagement sessions with the banks. According to Armizan, the amendments to the Act that took effect on June 1 introduced the reducing balance method and effective interest rate, replacing the flat interest rate and “Rule of 78” method.

items.title: Malaysia aims to finalise new e-commerce Bill this year, says domestic trade minister
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Sept 19 — The government aims to finalise the drafting of a new e-commerce Bill this year, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. He said the ministry had approved the policy decision to repeal the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 and replace it with a new, more comprehensive law. However, he said the process would require coordination between ministries as well as extensive engagement with stakeholders, including e-commerce platforms, service providers and industry players.

items.title: Malaysia records 102 deceased organ donors so far in 2026, but 12,575 still await transplants, says MOH
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 19 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) recorded 102 deceased organ donors from January to August this year. Deputy Director-General of Health (Medical) Datuk Dr Azman Yacob said this is an increase from the 89 deceased organ donors in 2025, equivalent to roughly 1.3 donors per million population. Meanwhile, Dr Azman said Terengganu was chosen to host this year’s MKPO in light of encouraging progress in organ and tissue donation across the East Coast states, reflecting growing public awareness.

items.title: DPM Zahid: Malaysia gets Indonesia’s green light to help battle Kalimantan fires behind haze
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Indonesia has given the green light for Malaysia to assist in tackling forest and land fires in Kalimantan that have caused transboundary haze affecting neighbouring countries, including Malaysia. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto gave his approval during their meeting at Istana Hambalang in conjunction with his working visit to Jakarta. Ahmad Zahid, also chairman of the Central Disaster Management Committee, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan was tasked with coordinating assistance with NADMA, APMM, the Malaysian Meteorological Department, RMAF, the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), and other relevant agencies.

items.title: Defence Ministry shortlists three missile systems for LCS, says Khaled
items.summary: LUMUT, Sept 19 — The Defence Ministry (Mindef) is in the final stage of shortlisting a surface-to-surface missile system from three countries to replace the system for the Royal Malaysian Navy Littoral Combat Ships (LCS). Without disclosing the three countries, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said several issues needed to be finalised before a government decision could be made. Meanwhile, commenting on the possibility of Malaysia acquiring the BrahMos air-to-surface missile system from India, he said the matter would be referred to the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) for study.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution says Home Ministry awaits Pardons Board letter, no Najib house arrest notification yet
items.summary: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry and Prisons Department had yet to receive the letter from the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department, which serves as the secretariat to the Pardons Board. Saifuddin said the letter would also clarify whether the Pardons Board had specified the premises where Najib would serve his reported house arrest, or whether the matter had been left to the Prisons Department. Currently, Datuk Seri Najib is serving his prison sentence.

items.title: AKPS steps up border security readiness ahead Johor Bahru‑Singapore RTS Link launch in January
items.summary: AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said preparations were being intensified through the use of technology, personnel training and operational simulations to ensure effective inspection of documents and goods. Mohd Shuhaily said AKPS would also advise operators on suitable technologies to enhance security and mitigate potential risks. Meanwhile, Mohd Shuhaily said 400 AKPS trainees were currently undergoing a three-month training programme at the Segamat Police Training Centre ahead of their deployment to the RTS Link.

items.title: Police seek Interpol help after six foreigners charged with Jalan Ampang Pavilion Embassy robbery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — Six foreign men were charged in absentia at the Sessions Court here yesterday with armed gang robbery at a residential unit in Pavilion Embassy here on Sept 7. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the charge was framed under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code, which carry a maximum sentence of 20 years’ imprisonment and whipping upon conviction. Fadil said the investigation papers were referred to the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Prosecution Office on Sept 17.

items.title: Preliminary report on Sarawak Flying Doctor helicopter crash due within 30 days, says deputy transport minister
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 19 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (BSKU) will issue a preliminary report on the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash on September 8 within 30 days of the accident, in accordance with Annex 13 of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) on Aircraft Accident and Incident Investigation. “BSKU will issue a preliminary report within 30 days from the date of the accident, in accordance with ICAO Annex 13,” he told reporters when met at a function in Long Lama on Saturday (September 19). Hasbi added that the BSKU was currently conducting a technical investigation in accordance with ICAO Annex 13 and Part XXVI of the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016.

items.title: Cloud seeding operation begins in Klang Valley after API readings exceed 150 for 24 hours
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The government, through the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), will conduct a cloud seeding operation in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya today and tomorrow to mitigate the effects of the haze and improve air quality in the affected areas. Nadma director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the operation was being carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department, Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), with an RMAF C-130 Hercules aircraft serving as the main asset. “The cloud seeding operation is scheduled to be conducted on Sept 19 and 20, following Air Pollutant Index (API) readings for PM2.5 in the affected areas exceeding 150 for more than 24 hours, based on readings by the Department of Environment.

items.title: Melaka Pakatan finalising talks with Bersatu, others to form PH Plus for state polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 19 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) Melaka is finalising negotiations with parties that have similar aspirations, including Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), to form a PH Plus collaboration to contest the Melaka State Election. Also present were Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, who is also Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, and Amanah deputy president Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa. Meanwhile, Adly, who is also Deputy Defence Minister, said the distribution of seats within PH among PKR, Amanah and DAP had been finalised, including the allocation of eight seats to Amanah.

items.title: Prabowo welcomes Malaysia’s offer of aircraft, helicopters and team to fight Indonesia fires
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has welcomed Malaysia’s offer to assist in tackling forest fires in the country, including through the provision of assets and expertise. He said the offer involved an aircraft, three helicopters and a firefighting team. Prabowo said Indonesia had also received offers of assistance from several other countries, including Japan, to help put out the prolonged forest fires, particularly in Kalimantan.

items.title: PM Anwar vows to strengthen pondok schools, introduce AI and modern fields
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 19 — The government will help streamline and elevate pondok institutions (traditional religious schools), including in terms of physical facilities, academic disciplines and the introduction of new fields of study suited to current needs, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The Prime Minister said that, as an initial step, several pondok institutions would be selected to pioneer new traditions of learning based on their respective areas of specialisation and tarbiah or disciplines. So children in pondok institutions must also be trained to master AI,” he said.

items.title: MACC says Najib’s conditional pardon has no impact on 1MDB case
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 19 — The status of the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case involving Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak remains unchanged following his conditional pardon, said Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman. He said each case must be handled separately based on the issues and investigations involved. Abd Halim said one case could not simply be equated with another, as each investigation involved different allegations and issues.

items.title: Perodua Alza driver dies after collision with Volvo trailer lorry near Sungai Tong in Terengganu
items.summary: BANDAR PERMAISURI, Sept 19 — A man was killed after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) he was driving collided with a trailer lorry at Kilometre 38 of Jalan Kuala Terengganu-Kota Bharu near Sungai Tong here last night. Setiu district police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the accident at 12.01am and identified the victim as Mohd Assfarizal Salim, 44, of Taman Balok Pelangi, Kuantan, Pahang. Zahril Asri said the lorry driver, who was travelling from Jertih to Kuantan, was uninjured, adding that police are investigating the case under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
